body:
Follow-up hardening from T46 (PR #56). NOT a known-exploitable bug today — the vector it closes is already closed by a different control — but it removes a class of risk rather than a single instance.

ESTABLISHED BY LIVE ATTACK DURING T46 (do not re-litigate)
- OPENCODE_CONFIG MERGES with local config rather than replacing it, and that merge includes project-local `opencode.json` from the working directory — which during a review IS the repository under review.
- With a FIXED agent name, a repo shipping an opencode.json that redefined the review agent with tools/permission granting write+bash won the merge, and the model wrote the file it was told to write. The sandbox was defeated by the diff it exists to contain.
- Current mitigation: the agent name is generated fresh per run (128 bits), so a file written before the run cannot target it. Verified: the same attack then fails. A hostile config that does NOT name our agent (top-level tools/permission instead) was verified not to broaden it.
- `--pure` is passed so the reviewed repo cannot load a plugin (plugins run code, which would make tool permissions irrelevant).

WHY THIS TICKET EXISTS ANYWAY
The random name defeats a config that targets the agent BY NAME. It does not remove project config from the merge at all. Anything opencode resolves from project config that is not agent-scoped — provider endpoints/baseURL, model routing, future config surfaces — remains repository-controlled. Running with cwd outside the worktree would remove the whole input rather than defending each use of it.

GOAL
Spawn opencode with a working directory outside the repository under review, while the reviewer still has the context it needs.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION — resolve before implementing
The reviewer currently has read/grep/glob/list so it can inspect the repo around the diff. `.omo` state was observed to follow the PROJECT dir, not the process cwd, so `--dir` does not separate them. Determine empirically whether opencode can be given a cwd outside the tree while retaining read access to it (`--dir`, an explicit path argument, or neither), and what that does to the read tools. If the two are mutually exclusive, this ticket becomes a tradeoff decision — isolation vs. cross-file review quality — and must be escalated rather than silently choosing one.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC1  Determine empirically whether opencode can run with cwd outside the worktree while retaining read access to it. Record the finding in a code comment. If it cannot, STOP and escalate with the evidence rather than picking a side.
AC2  If it can: spawnWithWatchdog/execCli gain a `cwd` option, applied like envOverrides — narrow, caller-supplied, never derived from the diff. Verified in test/exec-watchdog.test.js.
AC3  A hostile project opencode.json that sets a provider baseURL (not just an agent block) does not redirect the review's model traffic. Verified with a PATH-gated test against the real binary asserting no request reaches the attacker host.
AC4  The existing T46 attack test (hostile config redefining the agent by name) still passes.
AC5  Read-only enforcement still holds: the prompt-injection e2e test in test/opencode-sandbox.test.mjs still passes.
AC6  README updated to describe the isolation and any capability lost.
AC7  npm test passes.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test
title: Isolate opencode from project-local config by running outside the worktree
